features: EVERYONE IN THEIR OWN HOUSE — No migration: the database is not touched. Every management page now checks that what you are opening really belongs to the building named in the address.

THE DEFECT: CHANGING ONE NUMBER IN THE ADDRESS WAS ENOUGH. Management addresses look like «/gestionale/12/tabelle/45». The program read those two numbers separately — it looked up building 12, it looked up table 45, and it never checked that table 45 was a table of building 12. Anyone with access to one building could reach another building's data by changing the first number: millesimal tables, financial years, units, cash accounts, instalment plans.

THIS WAS NOT OPEN ACCESS FROM OUTSIDE: you still had to be logged in with a valid account and hold the permission for that kind of page. What was missing was the boundary between one building and another — which is exactly the boundary a firm works with when it manages several buildings, or when it hands one building to a colleague and not the others. Some pages had a hand-written check in their own code, 29 out of 112; the others did not, and above all every new page was born without one, because the check depended on whoever wrote it.

THE FIX: THE CHECK LIVES ON THE ADDRESS, NOT IN THE PAGES. The link is now declared once, on the address, and applies to everything that goes through it: the child is looked up inside the parent, and if it is not there the page answers «not found». That is 159 management addresses out of 160. The answer is «not found» rather than «not authorised», and that is deliberate: it does not even confirm that the resource exists somewhere. All 29 hand-written checks stay, because they protect against different things — the new one protects the address, the old ones protect what the page does afterwards with the data coming from the form.

THE ONE ADDRESS THAT STAYS OUT is the movement detail of a single expense item, where the link between financial year and item runs through three hops and cannot be expressed in this form. There the hand-written check is in place, and it is declared in writing inside the automated guard, so that it stays the only exception instead of becoming the first of a series.

FIVE PAGES THAT ANSWERED «ERROR 500» HAVE BEEN REMOVED. While looking for the addresses to bind, five turned up that had been generated automatically for pages that were never written: the detail view of a block, a stairwell, a table, a financial year and a management period. The code behind them was empty, and on a nested address that emptiness did not return a blank page but a 500 error to anyone who typed the address. No page linked there, so the defect was silent: it is the same family as the four removed in beta.48 and the two in beta.61.

UNDER THE BONNET: three new links between the data, which did not exist before and now make verifiable what could previously only be assumed — from the financial year to its charts of accounts and its instalment plans, and from the building to all of its expense items. A new automated guard with twelve checks verifies three separate things: how many addresses are bound and that the exceptions are only the declared ones with their stated reason; that every declared link points at something that really exists, because a renamed link would not raise an error but a 500 on legitimate requests; and that another building's data really is refused while your own really is served. Nine test files were also corrected: they built a financial year without attaching its management period, a state the program cannot produce.
